note: Scripted opening turn for the Functional Analysis unit 1 tutorial, used offline and in tests. Cites only evidence tags the service supplies (E1 = lecture 1 notes, definition of a norm; E2 = lecture 1 notes, sup norm on C_∞(X)).
text:
Before the exercise, tell me what you remember about norms in finite dimensions. In particular: in $\mathbb{R}^n$, if $\|\cdot\|_a$ and $\|\cdot\|_b$ are any two norms, is there a constant $C$ with $\|x\|_a \le C\|x\|_b$ for all $x$?

{source-backed} The notes define a norm on a vector space by the three properties (definiteness, homogeneity, triangle inequality) and note that the metric $d(v,w)=\|v-w\|$ makes a normed space a metric space [E1]. On $C([0,1])$ the sup norm $\|u\|_\infty=\sup_x|u(x)|$ is one such norm, and convergence in it is uniform convergence [E2].

{derived} The exercise asks you to compare that norm with the integral norm $\|f\|_1=\int_0^1|f|$ on the sequence $f_n(x)=x^n$. Compute both norms for a general $n$ first; do not reach for a conclusion about equivalence until both are written down.

When you have the two numbers, say what the ratio $\|f_n\|_\infty/\|f_n\|_1$ does as $n\to\infty$. Established so far: the setting. Next step: compute $\sup_{x\in[0,1]} x^n$ and $\int_0^1 x^n\,dx$.
